input.question: Which award did Janina Bil receive?

documents.text: As the sun set over the war-torn streets of Warsaw, Janina Bil made her way through the rubble-strewn alleys, her heart heavy with the weight of her mission. She had been working tirelessly with the Polish resistance, using her skills as a nurse to tend to the wounded and her bravery to smuggle Jews to safety. It was a dangerous game, one that could cost her her life at any moment. But Janina was undeterred. She had seen the worst of humanity, and yet she still believed in the best. She had lost count of the number of times she had risked her own life to save others, and yet she continued to do so, driven by a fierce determination to make a difference. As she turned a corner, she spotted a figure waiting for her in the shadows. It was Captain Jameson, a British officer who had been working with the resistance to coordinate their efforts. He was a tall, imposing man with a kind face and a sharp mind, and Janina had come to trust him implicitly. "Janina, I have some news," he said, his voice low and urgent. "The British government has taken notice of your work. They want to recognize your bravery and selflessness." Janina's heart skipped a beat. She had never sought recognition, only to do what was right. But Captain Jameson's words sparked a glimmer of hope within her. Maybe, just maybe, this could be the turning point they needed. "What does it mean?" she asked, her voice barely above a whisper. "It means you'll be receiving the Distinguished Service Order," Captain Jameson replied, his eyes shining with pride. "It's one of the highest honors the British military can bestow. You'll be the first Polish citizen to receive it." Janina felt a lump form in her throat as she processed the news. She thought of all the people she had helped, all the lives she had touched. It wasn't about her, she knew. It was about the cause, about the fight against oppression and hatred. But as she looked at Captain Jameson, she saw the sincerity in his eyes, and she knew that this award was more than just a recognition of her bravery. It was a symbol of hope, a reminder that even in the darkest of times, there were still people who cared, who fought for what was right. And as she accepted the news, Janina felt a sense of pride and purpose wash over her.
